title: The teaching is the refuge
hook: after the Buddha's death Ananda says the dhamma is their refuge

segments.voice: Yesterday: the accountant's step-by-step training, and your line, the walking is yours.

When a founder dies, one question comes fast: who's in charge now? Bands face it, and family businesses. The hundred and eighth discourse of the Middle-Length Sayings is set just after the Buddha's death. Ananda, his attendant, is in the city of Rajagaha. The kingdom is nervous; the city's walls are being strengthened against a rival king. And a powerful minister named Vassakara comes to ask Ananda exactly that question. Who leads you now?
screen: `WHO'S IN CHARGE NOW?` → `RAJAGAHA, JUST AFTER THE BUDDHA'S DEATH.` → `A MINISTER ASKS ANANDA.`

segments.voice: It starts with a smaller question. Ananda visits a brahmin named Gopaka Moggallana at a building site. Is there any monk, Gopaka asks, who has every quality the Buddha had? No, says Ananda. The Buddha found a path that wasn't known; his students only follow it. Then Vassakara arrives and presses harder. Did the Buddha appoint a monk to be your refuge after him? No. Did the community choose one? No. Then you have no refuge. So what keeps you together? Ananda turns the question around. We are not without a refuge, he says. The teaching is our refuge. Then he gets practical. There's a training code, recited together on the moon days. Whoever has slipped says so, and the group handles it by the teaching, not by anyone's favor. No monk gives the orders; the teaching does. That doesn't mean nobody is respected. Yes, Ananda says, they honor certain monks, but for what they live: virtue, learning, contentment, stillness and insight. Respect follows the practice, not a title. This fits what the Buddha said near the end of his life, in another discourse: be islands to yourselves, with the teaching as your refuge. Ananda isn't improvising; he's doing what he was told. Monastic communities still gather to recite a shared code together. When the founder is gone, the refuge is what he left in their hands.
screen: `NO ONE HAS ALL HIS QUALITIES` · `NO APPOINTED HEIR` · `THE TEACHING IS OUR REFUGE` · `RESPECT FOLLOWS PRACTICE` · then, large: `THE TEACHING IS THE REFUGE.`

segments.voice: Let the breath arrive on its own, and bring to mind one teaching from this year that has stayed with you, a line, a simile, a story. Don't think about who said it or who's in charge of it; let it sit in your chest like something you own. If you say the refuges, you might recall them quietly now; if not, just rest with the line.
Dhammappatisarana. Having the teaching as refuge: after the Buddha's death, with no appointed heir, Ananda tells a minister the community stands on the teaching itself.
Your line: respect follows the practice. The teaching you already have is the refuge. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Theravada monastic communities recite the Patimokkha, the training code, together on the new-moon and full-moon observance days, and seniority and respect within the community rest on ordination and conduct rather than on a single appointed leader of the whole tradition.

original.note: Pali dhammappatisarana: having the teaching as refuge. Ananda's word for the community after the Buddha.

trapdoor: what you thought: when a teacher dies, a successor takes over.
what it means: in MN 108, no one is appointed; the community stands on the teaching and the shared code.

what a scholar hears: the Gopaka-Moggallana Sutta is set just after the Buddha's death, while Rajagaha is being fortified, and it echoes his last instruction to make the dhamma one's island and refuge.
recall: in harmony, like milk and water

chat.says: Who led the Buddha's community right after he died?
options: In this discourse, Ananda says no one was appointed: the teaching is their refuge.
Ananda himself, named by the Buddha as the new head of every monk.
A council of brahmins, picked by the king's minister Vassakara himself.
chat.meaning: In MN 108 Ananda tells Vassakara no monk was appointed or chosen; the community stands on the teaching as its refuge.

Vassakara.meaning: a powerful minister who asks who leads the monks

Gopaka Moggallana.meaning: a brahmin Ananda visits at a building site

Middle-Length Sayings.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's discourses, the Majjhima Nikaya

sources.ref: Digha Nikaya 16, Mahaparinibbana Sutta (be islands to yourselves, the dhamma as refuge)

notes: MN 108 paraphrased. Confirm the setting: shortly after the parinibbana, Rajagaha fortified against King Pajjota, Ananda visiting Gopaka Moggallana's workplace.
Confirm the list of the ten qualities summarized here as virtue, learning, contentment, stillness and insight.
The 'be islands' instruction appears in DN 16 (and SN 47 suttas); the script places it 'near the end of his life, in another discourse', not as his last words. Confirm.

Review pass: the ten qualities Ananda lists in MN 108 include the jhanas and several supernormal knowledges; 'stillness and insight' is a compression. Also 'no single head of all Buddhism' is accurate, but some national sanghas and lineages do have heads (e.g. a Sangharaja); a Keeper may want that nuance.
Confirm 'dhammappatisarana' as MN 108's term and its Devanagari.
